text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The government has amended the terms of a forthcoming tender of the Tyumen Oil company, after some officials said that the sale could favour certain bidders.
- AO Lensvyaz has announced details of its investment projects, expected to raise about $40 million.
- SBS-Agro bank has launched Eurobonds totalling $250 million.

- A forthcoming meeting of the board of directors of Krasnoyarsk Aluminium plant, which currently accounts for four percent of the world output of primary aluminium, is expected to put an end to a long-running row within the administration.
- Two of Russia's most influential bankers have been accused by prosecutors of being involved in the embezzlement of $237 million in budget money.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chrnomyrdin declared a 1996 income of 46 million roubles ($8,000), and overall property and other holdings together with his wife worth 268 million ($46,000).
- Former Chechen field commander Shamil Basayev, who led a hostage-taking raid on a Russian town in 1995, said he had resigned as a deputy prime minister of the separatist region.
SEVODNYA
- The system of tolling deals, widely used in Russia's aluminium industry, will be gradually abolished by 1998, Head of the State Tax Service Alexander Pochinok is quoted as saying.

- Chief editor of Russia's liberal daily, Izvestia, Igor Golembiovsky, announced his resignation after failing to regain control over the paper in a long struggle against Izvestia's biggest investors, which are LUkoil and Uneximbank.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Foreign investors continue their struggle for control over Russia's big steelmaker, Novolipetsk Metallurgical Combine.
- Radical communist movements and political parties are planning a massive protest action in Moscow on July 18.
IZVESTIA
- Systematic shortages of food and fuel are bringing Russia's north to the edge of catastrophe.
- NATO's eastwards expansion will give a powerful impulse to the struggle for new arms markets.
- President Boris Yeltsin has signed two decrees to change the system of state control of the oil business in Russia.
- On a small Far Eastern island, Russian youth are enthusiastically training to join local criminal groups.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- Social benefits paid to various groups of Russian citizens are an enormous burden for the budget.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- Most of the bills vetoed by President Boris Yeltsin either contradict existing laws or represent the interests of narrow lobby groups, says the president's administration paper.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, + 7095 941 8520.
